# opencode-next-prompt

Predicts the message you are about to send and puts it in the prompt, so you can send it with one keypress.

When OpenCode finishes a reply, the plugin asks a model what you would say next and writes that suggestion into the input as a gray hint. Press one key and it becomes your message.

## Requirements

- OpenCode **≥ 2.1.4** (V2 plugin API)
- A model that can serve predictions. OpenCode Zen free models (`opencode/*-free`) cannot — see [Limitations](#limitations)

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-next-prompt
```

Or add the package to the `plugins` array of your `opencode.json` / `opencode.jsonc` (project or global):

```json
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-next-prompt"]
}
```

Restart OpenCode. The plugin brings no dependencies of its own; OpenCode provides the host packages.

## Usage

The suggestion appears in the input, in gray, prefixed with the accept key:

```
 [→] Now run the tests and fix the one that fails
```

Press **→** (or your own key) while the input is empty to insert it. With text in the input, the key keeps its normal cursor behavior. The ` [→] ` marker is a visual hint only — the inserted text is the suggestion itself.

The suggestion belongs to the reply it was predicted for:

- Typing, opening a dialog, or switching to the shell prompt only hides it. Clear the input, close the dialog, or come back to the prompt and it is still there.
- Accepting fills the input without consuming it, so deleting the accepted text reveals the same suggestion again.
- A new turn, a revert, a compaction, or a session switch discards it.
- A pending permission or form dialog, or a queued message, means the next action is already decided — nothing is predicted for that turn.

## Configuration

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-next-prompt",
      "options": {
        "acceptKey": "right",
        "timeoutMs": 20000,
        "model": "my-provider/fast-model",
        "variant": "low",
        "includeToolContext": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `acceptKey` | `right` | Key that accepts the suggestion. Only effective while the input is empty. Invalid values fall back to the default with a warning |
| `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Per-prediction timeout, 1000–300000 ms. A timed-out call is aborted; there is no retry |
| `model` | unset | Model used for predictions, as `provider/model` or `provider/model#variant`. A bare model id uses the session's provider. See [Choosing a model](#choosing-a-model) |
| `variant` | auto | Reasoning effort for predictions. By default the lowest variant the model supports is picked (`none`, `minimal`, `min`, `low`); set it explicitly (e.g. `"high"`) to override, or `"default"` to turn variants off |
| `includeToolContext` | `false` | Send the last completed tool's input and output to the prediction model. The tool's name and success or failure are always included |

Unknown providers, models, and variants are reported with an error toast instead of running a prediction with the wrong model.

### Choosing a model

The prediction model is resolved in this order:

1. the `model` option above
2. `agents["next-prompt"].model` in `opencode.json(c)`
3. `agents.title.model` in `opencode.json(c)`
4. the model of the current session

A dedicated agent keeps the prediction model separate from your chat model:

```jsonc
{
  "agents": {
    "title": {
      "model": "my-provider/fast-model"
    },
    // Optional dedicated override for the suggestions:
    "next-prompt": {
      "model": "my-provider/fast-model",
      "hidden": true
    }
  }
}
```

The accept command is registered as `opencode-next-prompt.accept`, so you can rebind it in `cli.json`'s `keybinds`.

## Cost and privacy

Every suggestion is one extra model call, sent to the prediction model — which may be a different provider than the one you are chatting with. The call carries the recent exchange: the latest reply in full, older turns trimmed to their last paragraph, code blocks collapsed to a line count. With `includeToolContext` enabled, the last completed tool's input and output go along too.

Your conversation is not modified. The prediction runs in a throwaway session that is deleted right after the call, and there is no retry: a failed or timed-out prediction simply produces no suggestion.

Debug logs contain session and model metadata, not your text.

## Troubleshooting

**No suggestion appears.** The prediction only runs when the session is idle — no pending dialog, no queued message — and the hint is only drawn while the prompt is focused, empty, and not in shell mode. Check that the prediction model is not an `opencode/*-free` model, and that `timeoutMs` is long enough for your model.

**Debug logs.**

```sh
NEXT_PROMPT_DEBUG=1 opencode
```

Logs are written to `$TMPDIR/opencode-next-prompt.log` (1 MB cap; rotated to `.log.1`). Set `NEXT_PROMPT_DEBUG_FILE` to a different path. Debug logging is off by default and can be turned off again once the issue is diagnosed.

## Limitations

- **OpenCode Zen free models (`opencode/*-free`) cannot serve predictions — this is an upstream bug.** The Zen free-tier gateway only accepts model requests that carry OpenCode's full default tool set, while a prediction deliberately strips every tool. Each prediction on a free model is refused with a misleading `Free usage limit reached` error and that turn shows no suggestion; the main conversation on the same free model is unaffected (tracked upstream as [anomalyco/opencode#49723](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/49723)). Configure a non-free prediction model (`model`, `agents["next-prompt"].model`, or `agents.title.model`) to use the plugin.
- The prompt has no slot for an inline hint, so the suggestion is drawn as the input's placeholder. This relies on OpenTUI's placeholder semantics; a host UI change can break it.
- Shell mode is detected through the keymap mode. If that changes upstream, verify that the accept key never inserts text into a shell command.
- Predictions are only generated for the focused session; switching to another tab or session starts a fresh prediction on its next turn.
